short_answer: Mike Lundin is an active handicapper on StatSalt, a pick site whose refund policy says all purchases are made from Wager Talk Media, LP. On 17 Nov 2026 his profile sold single plays, three day sport passes and all sports passes, and it showed plays graded as recently as 16 Nov 2026. In that narrow sense he is a real, current seller.

Whether his picks make money over time is a separate question. The sales copy leans on short runs such as "20-8 (71%)" in college basketball this season and "Profits 5 of the last 6 NBA seasons," all published by the site that sells him. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick kept by anyone else.

We also found almost no buyer talk about him anywhere. Treat him as an unproven seller, start with the cheapest option if you try him at all, and record every pick yourself with the line and time you got it.

guarantee: We saw no guarantee on his passes. The StatSalt refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold "as is"," and that once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed, no refunds will be issued. Its FAQ answers "Are your picks guaranteed to win?" with "No picks or predictions are guaranteed."

The page code for his single plays also lists a "guaranteed" option at $8, but the profile we read did not explain what that option returns. In this network a guarantee usually means site credit, not cash. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and they are usually far larger than the package price.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Mike Lundin pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Mike Lundin performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the runs on his page sit at about 65% to 71% winners. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Mike Lundin is close to nil. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no buyer who posted a review, a complaint or a tracked result of Mike Lundin's paid picks. Web searches for his name returned only his own StatSalt pages and unrelated people with the same name. Our saved Reddit archive had no posts or comments naming him, and a fresh Reddit archive search only worked for one betting forum, so the Reddit search was partial. StatSalt shows no reader comments or star rating on his profile. There is no pattern to report in either direction.

His StatSalt profile shows a recent 13 and 7 run over his last 20 plays and season run claims in college basketball and the NBA. These are published by the site that sells his picks, so they are marketing, not independent evidence.

TheRX daily service play thread tells members not to post picks from a list of services that starts with "All Wagertalk Cappers." Neither StatSalt nor Mike Lundin is named, and the rule gives no reason, so it says nothing about his quality.

We found no thread about Mike Lundin on Reddit, TheRX, Covers or Sportsbook Review, and no review on an independent site. The Reddit archive search of r/SportsBettingPicks returned no posts; searches of r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting timed out and could not be completed.

conflicts: Every record on the StatSalt profile is graded and published by StatSalt, which sells the picks. The "#1 ranked" claim compares him only with other StatSalt handicappers.

strengths: Prices are published for every option, and single plays were cheap at $5 on the day we checked.
The profile shows recent losing plays as well as wins, with the odds and the sportsbook for each.
Each play comes with a written explanation of the angle behind it.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw comes from the site that sells him.
No independent buyer reviews or complaints at all, so there is nothing to weigh either way.
All sales are final, and the guarantee option on single plays is not explained on the profile.
Sales copy uses words like "CAN'T MISS" and short season runs that prove little.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A run in a listing title is not a record.
Count units, not wins. His plays are rated 3 or 4 units, so a few big losses can erase many small wins.
Read the refund policy before paying. On StatSalt all sales are final.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Start with a single play or a one day pass before any monthly pass.
faq: He is a real, active handicapper whose picks are sold on StatSalt at published prices. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only records come from the site that sells them, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.

On 17 Nov 2026 his StatSalt profile sold single plays for $5.00 and all sports passes for $39 a day, $69 for 3 days, $99 for 7 days and $299 for 30 days, plus $49.00 sport passes.
Does Mike Lundin have a verified record?
No. His page shows short runs such as 20 and 8 in college basketball and a last 20 plays list, all graded by StatSalt. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.
Single plays are cheap enough to test him, and each comes with a write up. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and all sales are final.
